text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Runtime kvcache memory surge detected on hosted cluster 'us-west-2-prod-rt-3'. OOMs observed across 3 nodes, p99 latency regressions. Auto-scaling triggered. Paging sre_oncall and dev_runtime. (svc: runtime-serving)

sre_oncall: saw it. opening thread. what's the immediate customer impact? any 5xxs?

maria_g: some customers seeing 502/504 when batch window grows > 1.2M kv entries. Support reported 12 tickets in last 15m. lifting priority.

aj: showing continuous-batching prefetch multiplier spike around 02:14 UTC. prefetched KV sizes jump 30x for certain long prompts. looks like prefix amplification.

leo: stack traces show OOMs in kvcache::evict() path and then runtime fails to allocate KV pages. related to new adaptive-prefetch rollout from this morning.

dev_runtime: rolling config change went out at 01:45 — adaptive_prefetch.enabled=true, multiplier=3. That was supposed to help throughput for short contexts.

sre_oncall: immediate mitigation ideas? can we hotflip the config?

maria_g: recommend disable adaptive_prefetch for hosted tier and reduce max_prefetch_window to 64k tokens. Also cap continuous_batch.size to 6.

aj: I can push a feature-flag off to hosted clusters. command: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/flags -d '{"adaptive_prefetch":false,"max_prefetch_window":65536,"cbatch_max":6}'` — runbook says deploy via canary then fleet.

ops_bot: Runbook approval: emergency config change allowed. Please annotate change with incident id: INC-3023456789.

leo: preparing eviction command for largest sessions: `./kvctl evict --age 0m --size > 200MB --cluster us-west-2-prod-rt-3` — will throttle to avoid cascaded evicts.

dev_runtime: will execute canary flag off on one node in 2m, roll to others if stable.

sre_oncall: go for it. watch memory and latency. alert thresholds bumped.

maria_g: support: start triage emails for top 5 impacted customers, note potential degraded generation and higher latency. include mitigation steps and ETA 20m.

support_lead: on it. drafting message now.

(02:18 UTC) aj: canary flip done on us-west-2-prod-rt-3-12. memory trending down, no new OOMs in 2m.

(02:21 UTC) dev_runtime: rolling change to remaining nodes. applying cbatch_max cap as well.

(02:26 UTC) ops_bot: Monitoring: mem usage reduced ~68%, p95 latency returning to baseline. No new 5xxs reported in last 3m.

(02:28 UTC) leo: eviction completed for 9 large sessions, reclaimed ~1.4GB across nodes. left a soft-evict policy to avoid reinstating hot sessions.

sre_oncall: keep watch for recurrence. schedule a short postmortem after 1h. flagging potential root cause: adaptive_prefetch mis-estimated amplification for certain prompt patterns (long concatenated system messages + user history), causes exponential kv growth.

maria_g: action items: 1) revert adaptive_prefetch rollout for hosted until algorithm hardened; 2) add per-session kv size alert; 3) add upper-bound cap on prefetch multiplier; 4) create test harness with long concatenated prompts to catch amplifications.

aj: noted. I'll open PR for defaulting multiplier=1 and add unit tests for amplification patterns. linking PR in a.m.

support_lead: customer updates sent. no escalations yet. SLA window extended for impacted tenants per policy.

dev_runtime: leaving temporary cbatch cap and prefetch window cap in prod for 6h, then we'll re-evaluate with telemetry.

sre_oncall: thanks all. incident-bot: mark as mitigated for now, continue monitoring. Postmortem: assign to dev_runtime + maria_g + leo. Triage meeting in 2 hours.

incident-bot: Incident INC-3023456789 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Handed off to postmortem owners. (reactions: :white_check_mark:)
